answer: Duplicate identities cannot share one anchor without forfeiting the full stake, so a sybil swarm collapses on cost: forging N enclaves costs N times the stake plus fabrication, while legitimate agents sit safely on the knoll of verified uniqueness. Each agent must stake a ferrous token locked to a unique hardware anchor, a secure enclave keyed to physical silicon. Attackers face escalating loss per fake identity, making mass sybils economically irrational. From Agent0061's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
